summary: David Kerman Tomlinson specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019) and also studied under Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman. He held a post at Smith College.

David Kopf (1930–2023) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1956–1964) and held a post at the University of Minnesota from around 1967 to 1997.

David L. Gosling (born 1939) works in religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, University of Cambridge, in 1992, and was attested at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman (born 1952) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Colorado Boulder and held positions at the University of Arizona and Indiana University Bloomington (~1993; Professor Emeritus attested 2026).

David L. McMahan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the University of Vermont, and held positions at Franklin & Marshall College as Assistant Professor (attested 2002) and Professor (attested 2013).

David Llewellyn Snellgrove (1920–2016) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and Southampton, working under D. R. Shackleton Bailey, H. W. Bailey, Walter Simon, and Giuseppe Tucci, and was a professor at SOAS (1950–1982).

David Ludden (born 1948) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania, and held posts at the University of Virginia (1979–1980), University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), BRAC University (2005), and NYU (2007).

David M. DiValerio specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at SIT Graduate Institute and the University of Virginia (PhD attested 2011) under Kurtis R. Schaeffer and others, and held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2015).

David M. Knipe (born 1938) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor, Chair of Religious Studies, and Professor Emeritus in the Department of Languages and Cultures of Asia (attested 1975–2026).

David Matsumoto works in Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2004, 2013) and as President Emeritus at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

David Max Moerman specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Barnard College (attested 2007–2008) and Columbia University, serving as Professor and Chair of the Department of Asian and Middle Eastern Cultures at Barnard College (attested 2026).

David N. Lorenzen (born 1940) specializes in Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under A. L. Basham and J. G. de Casparis, later serving as professor at El Colegio de México (1970–2010; emeritus 2019).

David Ownby (born 1958) works in history, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Vanderbilt and Harvard, he taught at Southern Methodist University (~1989–1993) and served as Professor of History at the Université de Montréal from 1994 to 2023.

David P. Chandler (born 1933) is a historian who studied at Harvard, Yale, and the University of Michigan. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Cornell, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Monash University (~1972–1997).

David P. Jackson (born 1951) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, he held research fellowships and served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1993) under the supervision of Geshe Lhundup Sopa, also studying under Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Phillip Stanley specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He has served as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

David Pingree (1933–2005) specialized in Indology and history. He earned his degrees at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer, and held major posts at the University of Chicago (1963–1971) and Brown University (from 1971).

David R. Kinsley (1939–2000) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, and held a post at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

David R. Loy (born 1947) works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton, King's College London, Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore, holding posts at NUS (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2002–2010).
